title: Opportunistic Looters
text: “…If we’d gone out to fish, that would’ve turned into a disaster too. There’s no telling if we’d have made it back alive.”
Gazing out at the ravaged sea, Older Sister nodded in agreement with Big Sister’s parent.

“True enough… If we hadn’t gotten that threatening letter, or had our fishing trip obstructed, who knows what would’ve happened… Is it strange that I can’t help but think the interference was almost like someone foresaw all this?”
Sharp intuition, just like Éclair’s father, I say.
“Oh my… I suppose so.”
Older Sister knew the truth, of course, but she was kind enough to keep quiet about it at my request. She turned her face toward the very direction I’d launched my skill from.
“Anyway, everyone! Let’s be glad we’re alive! And now, let’s check the extent of the damage!”
“Right!”
“We should report this to the lord of the neighboring town too!”

And with that, they all seemed to head off to assess the damage. Well… after going to all this trouble setting the stage, it’d be a real problem if things didn’t work out smoothly, I say. Now then, what should I do next? I supposed I’d need to prepare to quietly deliver some valuables for the reconstruction effort, as a sort of unspoken apology…
“Nothing else is going to happen, right?”
Big Sister asked timidly, turning to the two who appeared to be her parents. The couple smiled gently at their trembling daughter.
“Yeah, I’m sure it’ll be fine now. Come on… let’s go home.”
“Oink-oink!”

With that, the pig who appeared to be Big Sister’s mother swung her notched machete back with a rough flourish before sheathing it with practiced ease. …Was it strange that the way she handled that weapon made her look thoroughly battle-hardened? Her footwork looked pretty nimble too, now that I noticed. If her level was high enough, I’d guess she packed some serious combat prowess. Fitting, perhaps, for someone who was both Big Sister’s parent and, by extension, Older Sister’s in-law. Well, they were Big Sister’s parents after all, and from what I’d heard, they’d drifted in from somewhere and settled in this village, so I figured they must’ve been adventurers or something along those lines originally.

Still, though… the father was a rear-guard mage, while the pig who seemed to be the mother handled the front-line warrior role. Older Sister possessed extraordinary skill and talent, and Big Sister, once raised up properly, would no doubt carry the same kind of strength. Perhaps it was only natural, given the bloodline. And yet… I’d heard that even with all that strength, they’d perished in the Wave. Without Older Sister’s help, they’d probably still managed to trade blows with the Dimension Kerberos, or at least worn it down significantly.

Now then… I considered just leaving the scene as it was, but… something nagged at me, like I was forgetting something. Some instinct inside me warned against leaving too soon. Best to stay cautious, I decided. I tried to puzzle out what exactly this unpleasant feeling was. For now, I headed toward town, to where Éclair’s father was.
“What’s the state of the damage?”
“There are many injured. Fortunately, only a handful of fatalities so far.”

Éclair’s father was asking Crocodile Guy about the extent of the damage. It seemed he’d had him running all over town checking on things. Crocodile Guy’s father, too, looked a bit worn out but was clearly alive and well, standing with arms crossed, keeping a watchful eye on his surroundings.
“There are fires burning, but we’re continuing the effort to put them out.”
“I see… but this… this disaster…”
“I believe this is what they call… the Wave.”
“Yes… there’s no other way to describe it. It’s a wonder anyone survived.”

Well, in truth, all of you actually did die, you know. Éclair’s father and the others appeared to be examining the Dimension Kerberos’s corpse. Meanwhile, the townspeople were working to grasp the situation while also tending to the wounded. Hmm… well, considering how things usually went in previous loops, the flow was: survive the Wave, then leave the rebuilding to the locals and the kingdom.

There we go! That meant Big Sister and the others were safe now! The immediate task was cleared, indeed! All that remained was to enjoy myself with the Filolial-samas while quelling the Waves, and this loop would wrap up without a hitch. It had been a lonely loop, not getting to see Filo-tan or Father, but I’d pulled it off! So all that was left was to make a dashing exit.

Just as I thought that, though… something tugged at the back of my mind, like I was forgetting something important. If I had to put a name to the feeling, it reminded me of that very first loop, when I’d watched Father off before moving on to the next one. …I couldn’t quite place what was bothering me, but my instincts were definitely nagging at me. I decided to take a bit more time observing the state of Éclair’s father’s territory.

While I was watching over the town with that thought in mind… Melromarc soldiers came marching in from outside, apparently as reinforcements. And right then, it clicked—I knew exactly what was about to happen.
“Oi! Kill the men, take the women and children alive!”
“Right you are!”
And so, well… it seemed the kingdom’s soldiers, along with some noble-looking fellow, had come storming in on a slave-hunting raid.
“What do you think you’re doing!”
Naturally, Éclair’s father came rushing over, face twisted with fury, shouting at the soldiers and nobles while bringing his own men along.
“Oh? If it isn’t Seaetto! Don’t you get it?”
Ha ha ha! The noble and soldiers let out a hearty laugh.

“The Wave, that legendary calamity sent to judge and destroy you Demi-Humans, has struck this place! All that remains is for us to deliver divine punishment upon the survivors and see to it that you meet the fate you Demi-Humans deserve!”
“Go!” the noble commanded, sending the soldiers charging at Éclair’s father and his people.
“You bastard… do you have any idea what’ll happen to you after pulling a stunt like this!”

Éclair’s father, Seaetto, said, his eyes sharpening with mounting rage. But the nobles, as if they’d never intended to listen in the first place, just kept laughing as they raised their weapons. This, I thought, was the very definition of foolishness.
“Damn it… the wounded haven’t even been fully treated yet.”
“How deplorable!”
A clash broke out between Éclair’s faction and the soldiers and nobles who’d come storming in… and the flames of battle began to spread.
“Haaaaaah!”

Crocodile Guy’s father swung his axe with tremendous force, sending members of the Three Heroes Church flying. But arrows and spells came raining down like a storm, and while Éclair’s father’s faction mounted their own counterattacks and defenses… more and more soldiers and nobles from the Three Heroes Church, convinced of their righteous cause, kept pouring in as reinforcements one after another. …Were these people idiots or something? I’d heard the damage from the Wave was terrible, but now I was witnessing with my own eyes that the Three Heroes Church’s looting was even worse. Should I just slaughter the lot of them? I was sick of merely watching. I’d been standing ready, intending to step in if Éclair’s father started getting overwhelmed, but I couldn’t just keep watching anymore.
“You bastards! What do you think you’re doing! Haaaaaaaaaaaaah!”
“Eclair!”
“Father!”

It seemed Éclair had rushed over just in time as well. Official reinforcements from the castle had apparently arrived too, but about half of those soldiers also began attacking Éclair and her father’s forces.
“Die, Seaetto!”
“The world will never accept you!”
“This is divine punishment!”
“Divine punishment, my ass! You’re nothing but looters riding on the coattails of disaster, you bastards!”

With a resounding clang, Éclair struck down the attacking soldiers one after another, protecting her father. Hmm… Father’s words about the moment people become most cruel crossed my mind. It was the moment they became utterly convinced of their own righteousness. It seemed the Three Heroes Church’s followers had convinced themselves that the Wave-stricken land… was punishment upon Éclair’s father and the Demi-Humans and Beastmen, who’d long been a thorn in their side, and that storming in here was nothing less than a righteous act—which was why they kept pouring in one after another. Could it be… that this battle would keep raging across Melromarc until Éclair’s father and his people were wiped out entirely? I couldn’t stand for that! Forget it, I’d had enough! I was going to wipe out the Three Heroes Church entirely! Just as I was about to unleash Aiming Lancer with everything I had, something happened.
“Drifa Chain Lightning!”
Crackle crackle crackle! Lightning magic chained through the attacking Three Heroes Church members.
“Gyaaaaaah!?”
“Abah, abababababa!?”
“Honestly… you’re all doing something incredibly tedious, aren’t you? Don’t expect Big Sister’s Big Sister to go easy on you either, okay?”
Older Sister had come rushing to the scene.
